correctness.rationale: For all positive moduli, the Ramanujan prime-power identity splits \(C(p^a)\) into \(p^{a-1}\) blocks \(p^{a-1}(pI_p-J_p)\). Unimodular column summation and row subtraction reduce each block to a rectangular \(pI_{p-1}\) over a row of minus ones, with determinantal divisors exactly \(p^{k-1}\) at all nonzero ranks \(k\). Hence the local Smith entries are \(p^{a-1}\), \(p^a\) and zero in the stated counts. Chinese remaindering multiplies the full difference kernels via tensor products of unimodular equivalences. For each prime \(p\), exactly \(\varphi(n)/(p-1)\) of \(\varphi(n)\) nonzero product entries have valuation \(a-1\), all remaining ones valuation \(a\). Primewise sorting yields the global divisibility-chain formula. Boundary \(n=1,2\), rank, cokernel order/exponent, cyclicity and modular kernel count follow. Exact SymPy Smith checks passed for 28 moduli through 42, supporting but not replacing the universal proof.

value.rationale: Determining the entire canonical integral Smith form for a natural arithmetic convolution at every modulus is a complete torsion/cokernel classification, not a finite census or mere rewriting of known Fourier eigenvalues. The theorem derives nontrivial exact torsion exponents, a complete \(\{1,2,3,6\}\) cyclicity criterion, and the exact number of modular null vectors for every modulus, giving meaningful arithmetic information unavailable from the complex spectrum alone.
